artifacts.title: cvprofiles
artifacts.summary: A Python package that treats construct validity as partial identification over a menu of measurement functions. Given a researcher-authored nomological network, the engine returns the admissible measurement set and a construct-identified range for a target functional — empty sets and wide ranges are reported as findings, not failures.
details: Pure numpy/pandas computation over score columns you supply: no GPU, no model weights, no API keys.
Inputs are four plain-text files — scores, roles, a nomological network with thresholds, and the target functional — so a profile is fully specified and replayable.
v3.0.0 ships the WVS/GPS patience application as a verifier-gated frozen run, with version tags acting as paper anchors.
Installable from PyPI (pip install cvprofiles); CI runs on every push.

credit.authored: The identification framing, the nomological-network protocol, the admissibility and gating rules, and the decision that empty sets and wide ranges ship as results.
credit.assisted: Agents implemented the engine, CLI, and reporting surface against that specification.
credit.verification: Frozen, tagged release runs with machine-readable proof summaries; CI on every push; synthetic-only claims labelled provisional rather than presented as paper results.

artifacts.title: LeanEcon v4
artifacts.summary: A clean-room rebuild of LeanEcon: an economics-formalization collaborator that takes an English claim through reviewed interpretation, Lean 4 formalization, and kernel-checked verification — emitting an auditable bundle and replayable trace instead of a bare "it compiles" claim.
details: A claim is only labelled VERIFIED when the formal statement compiles in a pinned Lean 4 + Mathlib workspace with no sorry and passes the full bundle validator, axiom audit included.
Interpretation and formalization run on Mistral models; semantic approval stays with an accountable reviewer under an explicit reviewer policy. Models draft, they do not certify.
Ships explicit non-claims alongside the promises: no autonomous VERIFIED, no production SLA, and a formalizer that is not yet statement-faithful.
First project to run the agent-attribution experiment: the hermes agent commits under its own GitHub account, so the human/agent split is recorded in the commit history rather than self-reported.

credit.authored: Product thesis, the verification contract (what VERIFIED is allowed to mean), reviewer policy, Core scope, bundle validator checks, and the explicit non-claims list.
credit.assisted: The hermes agent harness commits implementation work under its own GitHub account; models rotate per task rather than defaulting to the most expensive frontier model.
credit.verification: Lean kernel type-checking in a pinned workspace, a 12-check bundle validator, axiom/dependency audit, and replayable run traces.

artifacts.title: Silicus TA 2.0
artifacts.summary: A Streamlit-based RAG teaching assistant that lets students chat with their course PDFs and get answers grounded in cited page excerpts. Professors manage the corpus from a protected admin console — uploading, previewing, and re-embedding materials in the browser — with OCR, embeddings, and generation handled by a cached Mistral pipeline.

collaboration_breakdown.human: Product design for the two-role UX (student chat vs. professor admin), RAG pipeline architecture (OCR → chunk → embed → cosine retrieve → prompt-pack), storage layout (per-course Parquet + meta), admin guardrails (duplicate detection, size cap, password gate), and deploy story on Streamlit Cloud.
collaboration_breakdown.verification: Manual QA on citation accuracy per page, duplicate-upload and size-cap checks in the admin console, and end-to-end deployment on Streamlit Cloud with live courses.

credit.authored: Coded the Silicus TA 1.0 foundation by hand in 2023; 2.0 is my rearchitecture — more flexible, more efficient.
credit.assisted: AI use in 1.0 was mostly research and parsing documentation. Largely outdated by 2026 standards, but revivable if anyone shows interest.
credit.verification: Manual QA on citation accuracy per page, duplicate-upload and size-cap checks in the admin console, and end-to-end deployment on Streamlit Cloud with live courses.
